clue.text: US president with comparatively small primate

parts.note: either of the two American presidents named Bush
baby as an adjective means smaller than the usual size, as in baby carrots

explanation.surface: A US president is pictured alongside a rather small monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby is a small nocturnal African primate, a galago, with huge eyes.

clue.text: Mostly obstruct coalition

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A political alliance gets in the way of most things.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties joined in a common political alliance.

clue.text: Disgusted by old pervert

parts.note: sick in the sense of fed up and revolted
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone is repelled by an elderly deviant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicko is informal slang for a person with perverted or deranged tastes.

clue.text: Idle talk from bishop, first to leave there drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A bishop chatters while the first guest heads off and the rest get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blether is Scottish and northern English for foolish, long-winded chatter.

clue.text: Pantomime character's single error? Keeps quiet

parts.note: Buttons is the page boy in the pantomime Cinderella; the apostrophe-s is part of the possessive reading
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A pantomime actor fluffs one line; perhaps he should keep his mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; Buttons is Cinderella's loyal friend. The parse reads Buttons' one slip; the answer re-divides as buttons one's lip.
explanation.definitionFit: To button one's lip is an idiom meaning to stay silent or say nothing.

clue.text: Ambassador on at head of embassy

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An envoy is stationed at the top of the embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy or emissary, especially one representing the Pope.

clue.text: Withdraw from other court

parts.note: CT is a standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A case is pulled out of a different court.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to take or draw something out, much as one withdraws it.

clue.text: Reptile snapped at gorilla

indicators.note: something snapped is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A reptile's jaws snapped at a passing gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' fits the reptile so neatly it reads as its action, not a signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of the Americas and China.

clue.text: Financial security obtained by a setter? Yes, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange fashion, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether crossword setting makes a person rich, and oddly says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts the solver to take alternate letters, but here it means strangely, so all the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for enjoying comfortable wealth with no money worries.

clue.text: Girl with rat producing a firework

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for with
a rat and a heel are both a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A girl and a rat somehow set off fireworks together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework pinned to a post, named after St Catherine's martyrdom wheel.

clue.text: Star and co-stars he'll cast in part of theatre

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A director promises to cast the star and co-stars in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like theatrical casting, but it signals the rearrangement; 'and' just joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra stalls are the front seats on the ground floor of a theatre, nearest the stage.

clue.text: Rings back to express disdain

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Someone sends rings back to show their scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it contemptuously as unimportant.

clue.text: Giant pheasant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth
second meaning: a large Asian pheasant with eyespots on its tail

explanation.surface: A huge pheasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant with eyes all over his body gave his name to the argus pheasant, whose feathers bear eye-like spots.

clue.text: What's always held by Sotheby's?

parts.note: surface reading: something an auction house keeps in stock, like a regular sale
setter's reading: the name is written with a punctuation mark before the final s, and it never goes away

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to ask about lots in an auction house; it actually points at the punctuation inside the printed name, which the question mark flags as a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive name is written with that punctuation mark, so the name itself always contains one.

clue.text: Missile's power staggered sailor

indicators.note: to stagger is to lurch unsteadily, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: The force of a missile knocked a sailor off his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris was the submarine-launched ballistic missile carried by US and British navies.

clue.text: Laws start to be broken in the end?

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Do laws start to be broken only when things finally go too far?
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final provocation, the limit beyond which one cannot go: that's the end.

clue.text: Device that spins back and forth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a machine part that turns round

definitions.note: describes the word rather than standing in for it
definitions.meaning: second reading: a word that reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A gadget that turns round, back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back and forth' seems to describe the motion of the device, but it says the word reads identically from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is any device or part that turns about an axis, and its spelling is symmetrical.

clue.text: Strange noises linked to opening of special sitting

indicators.note: strange means odd and unfamiliar, so these letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Odd sounds are heard at the start of a special meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period when a body such as a court or parliament sits for business.

clue.text: A whole number, for example, located in Bury?

indicators.note: located in places one item inside the other

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Is a whole number, say, to be found in the town of Bury?
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, and its capital letter pushes the reader that way; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number with no fractional part.

clue.text: Obsessive enthusiast meeting old actor? Hazel, perhaps

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A superfan meets an old actor, perhaps called Hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel reads as a woman's name, but it is the plant; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel bears hazelnuts, so it is one example of a tree that produces nuts.

clue.text: Hard-working types, twenty-four at each end, with Jason, at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are scrambled
each end of a word means its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of twenty-four

explanation.surface: Hard-working crew members, Jason among them, sail round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Jason and the sea call up the Argonauts, a set of Greek heroes, but the heroes needed are on the Trojan side.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is an idiom for working very hard, so Trojans are hard workers.

clue.text: Do exam again, one among the others

indicators.note: among places one thing in the midst of another

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One student must retake the test while the others have passed.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination again after failing, a British term for retaking.

clue.text: Rack was knocked over by animal

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way round

explanation.surface: A rack was knocked over by a passing beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Rack looks like the verb or a torture device; it is a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a frame or trestle on which wood is supported for sawing.

clue.text: Plinth about to be taken in by individual

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside something else

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A statue base is about to be accepted by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is a low plain block forming the base of a column, wall or statue.

clue.text: Shore bird in difficulty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sandpiper found on coasts

explanation.surface: A wading bird finds itself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a stocky wader, and a tangle or hard problem is also called this word.

clue.text: Bird in rifle range once shot by foremost of pistoleers

indicators.note: shot means ruined and broken, so the letters are rearranged
the foremost part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird on a firing range was once shot by the leading gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' fits the gunmen in the scene, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey, famed for its diving stoop.

clue.text: King's terrible dread about onset of war

indicators.note: terrible means dreadfully bad, so the letters are thrown into disorder
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monarch is terribly afraid as war begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of eight English kings, so it serves as a king.

clue.text: Veteran soldier in TA, slowed remarkably

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something unusual, so the letters fall into an unusual order

explanation.surface: An ageing soldier in the Territorial Army has slowed down noticeably.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sweat is British slang for an experienced soldier or long-serving hand.
